title: Run it yourself, or get a cluster
summary: Use the hosted playground, run it on your machine against a local MongoDB, or point it at a real Atlas cluster: your own free one, or a temporary ephemeral one. Agents can use it over MCP or the REST API.

atlasRegister.note: Free forever M0 cluster (512 MB). No credit card. Every link back to mongodb.com carries the same UTM parameters (listed under utm).

note: Atlas CLI flags change between releases: check `atlas <command> --help` before relying on these.

options.title: Use the hosted playground
options.summary: Nothing to install. The web app, the REST API and the MCP server are the same service.

steps.label: Run a script through the API
steps.command: curl -s -X POST {origin}/api/v1/run -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"script": "db.collection.find({age: {$gt: 40}})", "config": "db = { collection: { documents: [{name: \"Ada\", age: 36}, {name: \"Linus\", age: 55}] } }"}'

options.title: Use it from an agent (MCP)
options.summary: A stateless Streamable HTTP MCP server. Tools: run_query, validate_query, explain_query, share_query, get_shared, export_playground, list_examples, get_setup_guide, get_limits.

options.title: Run locally with the Atlas CLI (no account, includes Atlas Search)
options.summary: A local MongoDB in Docker with Atlas Search and Vector Search, then the API and web app on your machine.

steps.label: Run the API (it also serves the web app)
Delete the deployment when you are done

options.title: Docker Compose
options.summary: The API, the web app and an Atlas Local MongoDB (search works) in one command.

options.title: Desktop app (Tauri)
options.summary: Runs queries in-process against a local MongoDB. No network service.

steps.label: Run it
steps.command: cd web && npm install && npm run tauri dev

options.title: Free-forever Atlas cluster (M0)
options.summary: A free cluster in your own Atlas account: 512 MB, no credit card, one per project. It stays until you delete it, so your data persists.

steps.label: Or from the terminal: sign in and create a free cluster
Optional: load the sample datasets (then use Data: Atlas sample data)
When you are done, delete the cluster if you do not want to keep it

options.title: Ephemeral Atlas cluster (temporary, expires in 7 days)
options.summary: A temporary free Atlas cluster created from the terminal. Atlas pauses it 2 days after creation and deletes it 7 days after creation unless you claim it into an Atlas account, which turns it into a normal free cluster with no expiry. Until it is claimed you can read and write data, but you cannot scale it, add database users or change network access. It runs on AWS us-east-1 and accepts connections from any IP address, so keep sensitive data out. This is a preview Atlas API: it can change, and creating one means you accept the MongoDB Cloud Terms of Service.

steps.label: Check that your Atlas CLI has the command (upgrade the CLI if it is missing)
Create the cluster. The request body is described in the Atlas Admin API docs; the response has the connection and claim details
Point the API at it, using the connection string from the response
steps.command: MONGODB_URI='<connection string from the response>' cargo run -p playground-api

steps.label: Keep it or let it go: claim it within 7 days using the claim details, or do nothing and Atlas deletes it. There is nothing to clean up
